decisions.reason: SOL turns 특별 into “specialized,” a narrower meaning the source does not support.
Captures 사내라는 것들 and 어디다 써 as spoken scorn better than BASE’s generic “who can do anything.”
Tighter prose that still keeps the dried-fish stringing image and the staggered line at the front.
갑니다 is that they are moving, not coming; BASE’s “coming” reverses the plea.
허 as a scoff and 정신 덜 들다 as “haven’t learned your lesson” fit the beating better than BASE’s dazed “senses.”
적당히 때려 is “don’t hit too hard,” and 가뜩이나 is “already so small.”
BASE’s “mouth waters” is stiff; SOL adds “Damn,” which 아따 does not warrant.
decisions.replacement: “Ah, my mouth’s watering just thinking about it… But what’s that?”

decisions.reason: 우뚝 멈췄다 is “stopped dead”; the gaze then sliding off the carriage is preserved.
Naturalizes 시선 끝에 without changing who they are looking at.
Same beat—he steps forward when the apparent leader speaks—with less translated bulk.
Closer to the clipped threat of 과객이라 and 요즘 같은 시기.
BASE loses 번들거리는 and 스스로; SOL’s “considered himself” makes a fact into vanity.
decisions.replacement: The oily gleam in his eyes said he himself was one of those dangers.

decisions.reason: 겨우 25레벨 is a mere Level 25, which BASE omits.
이야 and 기막힌 미녀 land better as “would you look at that” and “stunning beauty.”
SOL drops 확인했다면, weakens 확인할 수 있었 to “might have noticed,” and adds “blessed.”
The clipped “poor one” matches 말씀이 짧다 better than repeating “family.”
Only a comma change; no real gain.
갈라진 입술 licked by a bandit reads as cracked lips, not split-open injury.
More spoken than “this is a place we’ve been staying in,” with 어쩌겠소 intact.
뭘 is “About what?”, not the padded “Do about what?”
성의 is a sincerity shakedown; “generosity” swaps the source idiom.
임자 is ownership, which the deed punchline needs; “first come, first served” drops that.
“Certified deed” naturalizes 부동산 내용 증명서 without losing the anachronistic legal gag.
Same bewildered turn and “as if any of them would know,” in cleaner English.
Keeps the whispering beat and stays consistent with the deed rendering.
증명 in context is proving ownership, and 풀어 주고 is untying the captives.
그런 거 없어 is “I don’t have any,” not a bare “No.”
시선이 … 향한다 is toward the empty hands; “dropped” adds a downward look.
너희 정도야 is contempt for their caliber, and “level” collides with System Level.
우습지 / 우스운 거야 is punchier as “isn’t a joke / you are.”
SOL turns 횃불을 향해 into “into the torchlight” and 잡혀 있던 into “under guard.”
미쳤나 as “lost your minds” is natural spoken English with the same insult.
SOL drops 격한 반응에 and intensifies 가져다 댔다 to “pressed.”
A wary bandit’s 아는 놈들인가 is a dropped-do question, not a formal “Do you.”
태어나서 처음 보는데 is spoken “never seen them,” not a stiff present progressive.
너무 갑작스러워서 나까지 당황 is cleaner as “so sudden that even I was caught off guard.”
The extra s does not help and blurs the later, longer 대혀어어엉 cry.
SOL adds “probably” and upgrades 구해 달라고 to begging.
SOL’s “ugly as sin” intensifies 못생긴 and drops 하나같이.
체형 as “built like” is the natural English for the goblin comparison.
SOL’s “since the tutorial Quest” loses that the memory is of the quest itself; BASE’s “came to mind” is flatter.
decisions.replacement: A distant memory suddenly surfaced. No, it wasn’t even that distant. It had happened only a few months earlier, during the tutorial Quest.

decisions.reason: Same former-subordinate fact in smoother apposition.
Trims “the situation” without changing who is watching from behind.
Wolhwa is asking him directly; “of yours, Young Master Jin” is the natural address.
우열 is which of the two is worse; “side” is an unneeded extra frame.
방금까지는 구해 줄 생각 is more natural as “a moment ago I’d been planning to save them.”
The desperate 버리실 생각이십니까 reads as “going to abandon us,” not a cooler “planning.”
착하게 살았습니다 is living good lives, not specifically honest ones.
SOL weakens 눈치 … 귀신이다 and replaces 오죽할까 with a milder “then again.”
쓰읍 is tsk, and 구하긴 해야 is “we have to,” not a weaker “I suppose I should.”
BASE’s “new men” is stiff; SOL’s “still better” weakens 훨씬 낫지.
decisions.replacement: They said they had turned over a new leaf after that day, and leaving them like this wouldn’t sit right with me. More importantly, former bandits were far better than active human traffickers.

decisions.reason: 대화를 들은 … 끼어들었다 is a clean “overheard us and cut in.”
BASE calques 인생 피곤하게; SOL’s “heard me the first time” misses 다 들어 놓고.
decisions.replacement: “You heard the whole thing. Why ask again? You sure know how to make life difficult for yourself.”

decisions.reason: 보자 보자 하니까 is the “I’ve let this go long enough” threat, not a trailing “but.”
달라붙는다 is clinging; SOL’s “pressed herself” changes the fake-fear gesture and drops 도.
무서워 is “I’m scared,” and 꼭 지켜 줘야 해요 is “you have to protect me.”
촉촉한 눈망울 stirs the instinct; SOL replaces moist eyes with shimmer and moves the cause.
나로서는 is explicitly the narrator, and the contrast with the men swallowing still holds.
늘었군 as “now I have one more reason” is more spoken without adding motive.
끈적끈적한 눈빛 causing the shriek is cleaner as a lecherous look.
SOL drops the 어떡해, 어떡해 repeat and upgrades 무서워요 to “terribly frightened.”
허허 is “Ho ho,” and 몸으로 대화를 나눠 is the author’s body-conversation joke, not “let our bodies do the talking.”
나 좀 보자 is “look at me first”; BASE’s “deal with me” over-interprets.
Same 찢어 놔야 threat in a more spoken “he’d never.”
문득 멈췄다 and 모습을 본 … 껄껄 웃었다 are clearer as halt then burst into laughter.
막상 싸우려니까 겁이 나나 is “lost your nerve”; the already-too-late taunt stays.
그러게 is “exactly,” and 큰일 났다 must stay milder than the later 좆 됐다고.
SOL’s “clearing” is unspecified, and “tore” intensifies 휘몰아쳤다.
찰나 as “the blink of an eye” is the natural English for that instant.
BASE’s “figure” humanizes 그것 too early; SOL’s “a moment later” pads 어느새.
decisions.replacement: Something swept past Wolhwa and me at terrifying speed and was already standing in front of the leader.

decisions.reason: 장내 is the whole scene, not “everyone present.”
A first, disembodied 차가운 목소리 reads better as “a cold voice.”
SOL pads with “after all” and weakens 이어질 to “might have.”
목숨만은 as “just let us live” is more spoken than repeating “spare.”
주저앉다 is collapsing in place, not sprawling.
“That single word” points back to “Quiet,” and 내리깔린다 as silence falling is natural.
시퍼렇게 is already “deep blue”; the comma-to-period change is churn.
SOL front-loads “back off” and adds “Now,” reversing 숨결 … 떨어.
The nested italic thought is translationese; the same 개처럼 맞다 wonder stays.
SOL drops 마른침; he swallows dryly.
SOL’s “someday” is not in 잘만 요양하면 다시 걸어 다닐 수는 있.
파악한 is the narrator sensing the window, not Qi Sense revealing it.
Same Familiar/Level 1 memory in more spoken narrator voice.
Cleaner syntax for the First-Rate living-corpse glance without losing 힐끗거리고.
피가 부족하신가 is blood-shortage humor, not thirst for blood.
저러다가 죽겠다 is dying in that state, not from being left “there.”
BASE is stiff on 죽어도 싼 놈; SOL drops 멀쩡한.
decisions.replacement: “Doesn’t he deserve to die? They were selling perfectly innocent commoners.”

decisions.reason: 그래도 옮겨 is spoken “move him anyway.”
SOL flattens 오가며 and 살인에 관한 문제 to a thinner “concerned killing.”
법과 질서가 존재하는 사회 is naturally “governed by law and order.”
그 대상은 is targets; SOL recasts it as “those enemies.”
분명히 그랬는데 is “I was sure that was the case,” not “at least that used to be true.”
큰 죄책감은 들지 않았다 is “hadn’t felt much guilt,” with the same NPC realization.
SOL drops 무림의 방식 and replaces 다만 놀랐을 뿐 with “all I knew.”
괜찮겠지 is “should be fine,” matching the speculative ending better than “maybe.”
어설픈 불자 흉내 is a half-baked Buddhist act, not merely an “awkward Buddhist.”
Direct “I shook off … and approached” is cleaner narrator English for the same action.
살려 주십쇼 to their 대형 sets up 구해 주려고; “spare me” turns it into a don’t-kill-me plea.
이 자식들은 as address is “you bastards,” matching the scolding 가만히 있어.
SOL omits 자유의 몸이 된 after the ropes come off.
은인으로 모시겠습니다 is serving him as Benefactor, not merely regarding him as one.
SOL turns 그나저나 into “more importantly” and flattens 그것도 다섯 명이 한꺼번에.
SOL drops 명색이 성인 남자다, the “adults in name” qualifier.
뭐지, 이놈들 keeps “these guys”; “them” is a pointless trim.
이상함을 감지한 is more idiomatic as “something off.”
The interrogation is already about the ghosts; “catch them” is the natural spoken form.
SOL explains the 십색귀 nickname joke that the Korean only fires as an exclamation.
눈알을 뒤룩뒤룩 is shifty darting eyes, not English “rolled their eyes.”
배운 게 그런 것뿐이라 is what they learned, not merely what they know.
BASE misses the 그, stammer; SOL’s “B-but” drops 그래도.
SOL’s “one last job and quit” overreaches 한탕만 치고 빠지자; BASE undersells 영 신통치가 않아서.
decisions.replacement: “We tried to work honestly, but nothing went right… We said we’d pull just one job and get out, but then…”

decisions.reason: 건드리지도 않았죠 is the stronger “never would’ve touched,” in spoken English.
익숙한 단어 is a familiar word, and 고민하던 is wondering, not a cooler “term/considered.”
저놈들이 뭐라고 asks what they said, not what the ghosts called them.
아 is “Ah”; “Oh” is mere synonym churn.
그래 is “yeah,” not a formal “yes.”
Same capture-then-Red-Wind-Band reveal without BASE’s awkward “some bunch.”
SOL drops 똑똑히; BASE’s “Didn’t I?” is the wrong force for 맞지?
decisions.replacement: “Yes. I heard it clearly with my own ears. Right?”

decisions.reason: SOL’s “chimed in” flattens 앞다퉈 한 마디씩 보태기 시작했다.
Restores 도 (“also”) while keeping the dawn departure.
마적 달려야 is riding without stopping, not generic travel.
그렇단 말이지 is confirmatory musing, not the question “Is that so?”
어제, 그리고 오늘 reads with better fragment rhythm as “Yesterday, and now today.”
Same two-day Red Wind coincidence and Saneum/Eung-hyeon geography in tighter prose.
이 녀석들 stays in “these men”; SOL’s “they” is a needless trim.
BASE calques 고개를 as a trembling head; SOL’s “tremblingly nodded” is awkward.
decisions.replacement: The human trafficker whose collar I held in my right hand—or rather, the mounted bandit from the Red Wind Band—nodded, trembling.

decisions.reason: 그 순간이었다 is the cut “At that moment—,” not BASE’s added “that was when it happened.”
The bird is first 매, a hawk; SOL names a messenger eagle before the 전서응 beat.
전서응 is the glossary term messenger eagle, not hawk.
분위기가 묘하게 돌아가는데 is “taking a strange turn,” not merely “getting strange.”
